scenario.title: 收到喜帖、參加婚禮、致詞
scenario.context: 第四章的收尾：好朋友要結婚了。從聽到求婚的消息、回覆喜帖、到婚禮上跟陌生人聊天，你會用到比較級、關係子句、條件句，也會用到這一章學過的轉述、稱讚和同理。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: OK, sit down. Leo popped the question last night!
lines.zh: 好，你坐下。Leo 昨晚求婚了！

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: No way! What did you say?

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: I said yes, obviously! We're tying the knot next spring.
lines.zh: 當然說好啊！我們明年春天要結婚。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I'm so happy for you! How did he do it?
lines.zh: 我真為你們開心！他怎麼求的？

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: At the café where we had our first date. It was the sweetest thing ever.
lines.zh: 在我們第一次約會的咖啡店，是有史以來最甜的事。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: That's such a Leo thing to do. Was he nervous?
lines.zh: 真的很 Leo 的作風。他有緊張嗎？

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: He told me he had been planning it for months and almost got cold feet twice.
lines.zh: 他跟我說他計畫了好幾個月，還差點臨陣退縮兩次。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Ha! Well, if you need help with the invitations, I'll design them for free.
lines.zh: 哈！嗯，如果你需要喜帖，我免費幫你設計。

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.en: Hi, I don't think we've met. How do you know the couple?
lines.zh: 嗨，我們好像沒見過。你跟新人怎麼認識的？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I'm Jess's friend from college. And you?
lines.zh: 我是 Jess 的大學同學。你呢？

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.en: I'm Leo's cousin. I came as my sister's plus-one.
lines.zh: 我是 Leo 的表哥，我是以我姊姊的攜伴身分來的。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Nice! Isn't this the most beautiful venue?
lines.zh: 不錯！這是不是最美的場地？

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.en: It is. And the invitations were gorgeous. Someone said a friend designed them.
lines.zh: 是啊。喜帖也好漂亮，有人說是朋友設計的。

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.en: No way! You must be so proud. They were such a big hit.
lines.zh: 真的假的！你一定很驕傲，大家都超喜歡。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Thank you, that's so kind of you to say.

patterns.en: How do you know the couple?
patterns.note: 婚禮上跟陌生人聊天的最佳開場

patterns.en: Let's raise a glass to the happy couple!
Wishing you a lifetime of happiness.

chinglish.right: Congratulations on your wedding! / Congrats on getting married!
chinglish.why: congratulations 通常用複數，後面接 on + 名詞 / V-ing。

chinglish.right: I'll be at your wedding. / I'll be there!
chinglish.why: join 比較像「加入團體或活動」，參加婚禮說 attend / be at / come to。

chinglish.wrong: If you will need help, I will help you.
chinglish.right: If you need any help, just let me know.
chinglish.why: if 子句不用 will（複習第 39 單元）。

chinglish.wrong: He is the man which she will marry.
chinglish.right: He's the man she's going to marry.
chinglish.why: 指人不用 which；當受詞的關係代名詞可以省略（複習第 31 單元）。

grammar.title: 比較、關係子句、條件句
grammar.oneLiner: 這一章的三個核心：比較級不疊 more、關係子句不重複主受詞、if 子句不用 will。
whenToUse: 比較級：much / way / even + 比較級；the + 最高級 + I've ever…。It was the sweetest thing ever.
關係子句：名詞 + who / that / which / whose / where + 子句；不重複 he / it。The café where we had our first date.
where 也可以當關係詞，接地點：the café where we met（第 87 單元會細講）。
條件句 type 1：If + 現在式, will + 原形。If you need help, I'll design them.
轉述：He told me he had been planning it.（第 32、36 單元的延伸）
must 推測、so / such 加強、tag question 拉近距離，都是婚禮閒聊的好工具。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 這一章的錯誤有一個共通點：中文把修飾語放在前面、用同一個詞表達各種程度、用「會」標示所有未來，所以台灣人很容易把中文的結構直接搬進英文。整合單元的目的，就是讓你在同一個情境裡切換這些結構，練到不用想就能說出正確的形式。

examples.correct: It was the most beautiful wedding I've ever been to.
examples.incorrect: It was the most beautifulest wedding I ever been.

examples.correct: That's the guy who caught the bouquet.
examples.incorrect: That's the guy who he caught the bouquet.

examples.correct: If it rains, they'll move the ceremony inside.
Their venue was much bigger than I expected.
She told me she had cried during the vows.

quiz.question: This is ___ wedding cake I've ever seen.
The restaurant ___ they got engaged is closing.
If you ___ (come) early, you can help us set up.
"We're getting married in May." → She said they ___ getting married in May.
The groom ___ gave the speech was hilarious.

examples.en: They're tying the knot in Kyoto next year.
examples.zh: 他們明年要在京都結婚。

examples.en: After ten years together, they finally tied the knot.
examples.zh: 在一起十年後，他們終於結婚了。

slang.usage: 喜帖或活動邀請中「可以多帶一位」。bring a plus-one / be someone's plus-one。

examples.en: The invitation says I can bring a plus-one.
Want to be my plus-one at the wedding?

slang.meaning: 臨陣退縮、緊張到想反悔
slang.usage: get cold feet，通常用在婚禮、重大決定前。

risk.note: 常見說法；說新郎新娘 got cold feet 帶八卦意味，要看場合。

examples.en: I almost got cold feet before my job interview.
examples.zh: 面試前我差點打退堂鼓。

examples.en: Everyone gets a little cold feet before a wedding.
examples.zh: 婚禮前每個人都會有點想逃。

examples.en: He's planning to pop the question on her birthday.
examples.zh: 他打算在她生日那天求婚。

examples.en: So when are you going to pop the question?
examples.zh: 所以你什麼時候要求婚？

review.question: If the weather ___ nice, the ceremony will be outside.
review.explanation: 複習第 39 單元：if 子句用現在式。

review.question: The bride did her own makeup. She did it all by ___.
It was ___ beautiful speech.
review.explanation: 複習第 37 單元：such a + 形容詞 + 名詞。

review.question: "I'll be there." → He said he ___ be there.
You've been planning the wedding for a year? That ___ be stressful.
review.explanation: 複習第 35 單元：must 表同理推測。

review.question: I'd rather ___ a small wedding.
review.explanation: 複習第 34 單元：would rather + 原形。

review.question: By the time we arrived, the ceremony ___ already started.
review.explanation: 複習第 32 單元：過去完成式。

review.question: They ___ a professional photographer take the photos.
review.explanation: 複習第 24 單元：have + 人 + 原形。

review.question: I can't go to the wedding. I have ___ flu.
Leo finally popped the ___ last night!
